Answer: B
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) progressing to dense, multifocal consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete radiological resolution within a short timeframe (Figures 5a/5b). This rapid progression and subsequent clearance are characteristic of alveolar hemorrhage (as seen in Weil Syndrome) rather than typical bacterial pneumonia or fibrotic processes, which would not resolve so completely and quickly.
